top_story: Trump’s March threat to destroy Iran’s power plants unless Tehran reopened the Strait of Hormuz set the basis for a wider confrontation that Iran had already signaled it would answer through regional escalation. That warning materialized on 3 June when Iranian strikes hit Kuwait International Airport, killing at least one person, wounding several others, and briefly shutting a critical civilian transport hub as smoke and fire disrupted movement and public confidence. On the same day, the toll of Israel’s campaign in southern Lebanon deepened as three hospitals were struck within a week, killing nine and injuring more than 150, mostly medical staff, further eroding civilian access to care near the border. The regional picture is no longer defined by deterrent signaling alone but by attacks on infrastructure essential to everyday life, widening the human and political costs across multiple fronts.
